answer.summary: Hari and LinkedIn turned an internal PM training bootcamp into a filmed course for a wider audience, building its curriculum around LinkedIn case studies. They learned that teaching product management takes practical examples and decision-making practice—not frameworks alone.

sections.heading: How they developed the course
sections.content: Hari had wanted to make a course partly to try LinkedIn Learning himself and understand the instructor experience, though he initially worried he might not have anything to teach. The effort grew out of an internal survey in which employees identified lacking job skills as a major pain point. Since LinkedIn had hired PMs without a PM degree and had done little formal training, the team created an internal “product university” bootcamp. After trying different models, they built a curriculum from LinkedIn’s own product work, then filmed the course and opened the bootcamp up to the world. The course includes internal LinkedIn use cases.

sections.heading: What they learned about teaching effectively
sections.content: They found that frameworks alone were not enough: effective teaching needed a series of case studies and real examples. The course teaches how to judge and validate a new idea, including setting a bar for evidence, prioritizing ideas against a pain point, distinguishing acute pain from a problem affecting a wider group, deciding what data would validate an idea, and using tools to assess the idea, check that the process was followed, and communicate the reasoning.
